title: Staggered capacity reservation and launch phasing for multi-service release train
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
Coordinate a phased launch for the combined runtime/console/API release train that reserves capacity across Dedicated pools and cloud regions, aligns canary windows in Console, and provides deterministic gating for API changes. The goal is to minimize customer-visible regressions while avoiding large, simultaneous capacity allocations that inflate cost.

Motivation:
- Previous launches saw either overly conservative capacity reservations (leading to high cost) or under-provisioning during staggered rollouts (leading to throttling and degraded latency).
- We need a repeatable playbook that product, runtime, and console teams can follow to synchronize: capacity commits, canary cohorts, rollback gates, and post-launch monitoring.

Scope:
- Work across runtime, console, and API surfaces to define a phased launch plan for multi-region deployments.
- Produce capacity reservation templates per region and per Dedicated pool tier, with guardrails for autoscaling and burst policies.
- Define canary percentages/time windows, telemetry dashboards, and automatic rollback triggers.
- Deliver a Console UI checklist for release engineers to mark gating criteria as satisfied.

Goals (success metrics):
- No customer-facing SLO breach during phased rollout (target: 99.9% token-latency SLO).
- Keep incremental committed capacity cost increase below 12% for the first 72 hours post-launch.
- Detect/regress performance anomalies within 15 minutes of a canary cohort reaching 10% of target traffic.

High-level timeline / milestones:
- 2026-02-18: Kickoff (this ticket created).
- 2026-02-26: Draft capacity reservation template (DEV + ENG review).
- 2026-03-05: Canary policy spec (canary percentages, duration, metrics) reviewed by SRE and Observability.
- 2026-03-12: Cross-team alignment meeting; final decisions recorded (see Decisions below).
- 2026-03-20: Dry-run with internal traffic on staging across 3 regions.
- 2026-03-28: Final sign-offs and scheduling of release train window (release window 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-02).

Rollout strategy / gating:
- Phase 0 (Pre-warm): Reserve 40% of anticipated Dedicated capacity in primary region (soft reservation). Validate autoscaling policies.
- Phase 1 (Canary A): Route 2% of production traffic to new release in region A for 30 minutes. Monitor token latency, error rates, and tail latency.
- Phase 2 (Canary B): If Phase 1 stable for 60 minutes, increase to 5% and expand to region B with identical metrics.
- Phase 3 (Ramp): Increase to 20% per region in controlled increments (10% every 30m) and validate cost telemetry.
- Phase 4 (Full): Open to 100% traffic once stability criteria for latency and error rates hold for 4 hours and cost delta threshold passed.

Gating criteria (must be explicit in Console checklist):
- No >0.5% increase in 95th-percentile token latency across canary groups for 60m.
- Error rate delta <0.1% absolute for core text-generation endpoints.
- No increase in request queue length beyond baseline + 2 std deviations in Dedicated pools.
- Observability and tracing instrumentation capturing full request lifecycle for sampled requests.

Rollback strategy & automated triggers:
- Automatic rollback if any gating criteria breached for a continuous 5 minute window during ramp.
- Manual rollback required if SLO variance persists >60 minutes after automatic mitigation.
- Post-rollback: immediate incident review and temporary freeze on similar changes until root cause identified.

Decisions made (meeting 2026-03-12):
- Use a central reservation API surfaced in Console to submit soft reservations and estimate cost impact. (Decision owner: PM/Product Ops)
- Canary windows will be enforced by the routing layer in the API gateway and observability alerts will be first-class gating signals. (Decision owner: ENG - Runtime)
- Default canary sizes: 2% / 5% / 20% / 100% by phase. Teams can request deviations with engineering approval.
- For Dedicated customers who opt into staged migration, allow namespace-level reserved capacity; otherwise route them to fallback compatible model variants during ramp.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Cost vs safety: bigger reservation reduces risk of throttling but increases committed spend. We will default to conservative soft reservations for the first 72h and convert to hard reservations only if utilization metrics are sustained.
- Complexity vs clarity: central reservation API adds one integration, but removes ad-hoc region scripts and reduces human error in capacity commits.

Dependencies and open blockers:
- ENG-2891: Routing layer support for cohort targeting must land (blocked until 2026-03-16).
- ENG-3027: Console checklist UI components (progress indicator + gating toggles).
- DES-412: UX copy and error-state designs for the Console reservation flow.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Phased+Launch+Playbook (draft)
- GH Project board: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-train/projects/11
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/893 (routing/cohort support)
- Observability dashboard (staging): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/launch-playbook/staging-canary-overview

Open questions / risks:
- Some enterprise Dedicated customers have strict blackout windows — need a per-customer opt-out flow for staged migration. (Action: Solutions Eng to collect list by 2026-03-18)
- KV cache warmup behavior across model variants might cause latency spikes for short-lived canaries. (Action: Research team to validate warmup script effectiveness in dry-run.)

Next steps / immediate actions:
- [Liam] finalize capacity reservation template and publish to Confluence (due 2026-03-15).
- [Eng leads] land ENG-2891 and ENG-3027 in staging for dry-run (owners: Maya R, Chen L).
- [Design] deliver Console checklist mocks and copy by 2026-03-16.
- Schedule a 30m launch rehearsal with SRE, Runtime, Console, and PM on 2026-03-18.

Progress updates (timeline of comments):
- 2026-02-18 (Aisha P): Ticket created; initial scope and outcomes documented.
- 2026-02-25 (Liam O): Drafted capacity reservation template; posted link to Confluence draft.
- 2026-03-03 (Maya R): ENG-2891 implementation in progress; expect PR early next week.
- 2026-03-08 (Chen L): Observability queries for canary gating added to staging dashboard; still tuning thresholds.
- 2026-03-12 (Liam O): Cross-team decisions captured above; moved to In Progress and scheduled dry-run.

Acceptance criteria (for this ticket to be closed):
- Playbook doc and Console checklist published and reviewed by SRE and Runtime.
- Dry-run executed in staging across 3 regions with no SLO violation and documented learnings.
- ENG dependencies merged to staging and tested.
- Launch window scheduled and communicated to customer-facing teams.

If anything changes in schedule or gating thresholds, we will capture it as an update here and notify stakeholders via the #release-train Slack channel.
